clue.text: Spring visitors in unseemly brawl at Queens

indicators.note: unseemly behaviour is disorderly, so the letters of brawl are thrown into disorder

parts.note: ER is the abbreviation for a queen (Elizabeth Regina), made plural

explanation.surface: Migrant birds arrive to find an ugly fight going on in Queens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unseemly' rearranges BRAWL to WARBL, followed by ERS for Queens.
explanation.definitionFit: Warblers are migrant songbirds that arrive in Britain each spring.

clue.text: B. Oddie oddly gave half away in wine shop

parts.note: the initial B is taken as printed

indicators.note: oddly picks out the letters in the odd-numbered places of the surname
with half away only the front half of the word gave is kept

explanation.surface: Birdwatcher Bill Oddie behaves strangely and gives half his money away in a wine shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of ODDIE, giving ODE; 'half away' leaves GA from GAVE. Bill Oddie is a British birdwatcher and TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish word for a wine shop or wine cellar.

clue.text: Biannual turning point in star's career

definitions.text: Biannual turning point in star's career

parts.words: Biannual turning point in star's career
parts.note: read as astronomy: the sun is a star, and twice a year its yearly path turns back at its northernmost or southernmost point

explanation.surface: A celebrity's career has a crisis twice a year.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a celebrity, but the star is the sun, whose apparent path turns at midsummer and midwinter.
explanation.definitionFit: The two solstices each year mark where the sun's apparent course turns back.

clue.text: Publicity fever here in spring 1968

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, that is, publicity
ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A promotional campaign and an illness strike during the spring of 1968.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prague Spring of 1968 was the Czechoslovak reform movement crushed by Soviet tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of the Prague Spring, the 1968 Czechoslovak liberalisation, is the place meant.

clue.text: In which female's ready to fertilise main offspring

definitions.text: In which female's ready to fertilise

parts.note: the main is an old poetic term for the sea
a son is a male offspring

explanation.surface: A fertile female and her offspring by the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal said to be in season is on heat, ready to mate.

clue.text: TV centre cut outside broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are rearranged
cut means the word outside is docked of its final letter

explanation.surface: A television centre trims its outside broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks OUTSIDE to OUTSID, and 'broadcast' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where TV programmes are made, the heart of a broadcaster.

clue.text: Spring course disrupted

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown out of order, so the letters of course are rearranged

explanation.surface: The spring term course has been disrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring here is a water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is where a stream rises, its point of origin.

clue.text: Central Mexico's team

definitions.meaning: the middle two letters of the word Mexico are X and I
a football or cricket side has this many players

explanation.surface: A side representing the heart of Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense works through Roman numerals: the centre of MEXICO is XI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football teams field this many players, so a team is called one.

clue.text: Before jump, guard (23) takes hours to unwind

indicators.note: Before tells us the guard word is placed in front of the jump word

parts.note: to keep watch is to stand guard
to spring is to jump

explanation.surface: A sentry poised to leap takes hours to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is SPIRAL: a watchspring is a coiled spiral that slowly unwinds to drive a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The coiled mainspring of a mechanical timepiece releases its stored energy slowly over many hours.

clue.text: Modest presenter of 8 in part exchange

definitions.meaning: swap the two parts of 8 to get Springwatch

explanation.surface: A modest TV host appears in a trade-in deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Springwatch is a BBC wildlife series; Kate Humble presented it alongside Bill Oddie.
explanation.definitionFit: Being humble means having a modest, unassuming view of oneself.

clue.text: False diagnoses nonetheless given out

indicators.note: a false reading is a wrong arrangement, so these letters are rearranged
read as none less: nought, the letter O, is taken away from diagnoses

explanation.surface: Wrong diagnoses were nevertheless handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' splits as none (O) less, so DIAGNOSES loses O; 'False' rearranges DIAGNSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks assigned are allotted or handed out to people.

clue.text: What subs do about sea change

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sub-editors on a newspaper edit copy

explanation.surface: Submarines diving around cause a change at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subs' are sub-editors, not submarines or reserves; 'about' turns EDIT round.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide is the twice-daily rise and fall of the sea, a regular change in its level.

clue.text: Bath physicist screamed ecstatically about his intuition at first

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters are placed around the others
someone behaving ecstatically is wild with joy, so the letters of screamed go wild
at first takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A scientist in the bath shrieks with joy at his sudden insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ecstatically' rearranges SCREAMED into ARC...MEDES, set 'about' HI, the first letters of 'his intuition'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek scientist famously grasped displacement while bathing and cried Eureka.

clue.text: Estimates property housing ship and crew

indicators.note: housing means containing, so property holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: assets are property owned
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a crew is made up of men

explanation.surface: Valuations are made of a property that holds a ship and its crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' signals a container; 'Estimates' looks like a verb but is the plural noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessments are evaluations or estimates of value or quality.

clue.text: 4 in Vermont, say, spend summer there

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Vermont is an example of an eastern US state, E plus STATE
four in Roman numerals is IV

explanation.surface: Four people in Vermont spend the summer there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals a container; 'there' means America, which spells the word without the A of British aestivate. Vermont counts as an eastern state.
explanation.definitionFit: To aestivate is to spend the summer dormant, the hot-season counterpart of hibernating.

clue.text: Rock group's third

definitions.meaning: in geology, a system of rocks laid down in one era

explanation.surface: The third album by a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: The rock group is not a band but a geological system of rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tertiary means third, and names a geological period and its rock system.

clue.text: Know them to grow them?

parts.note: plays on the idiom know your stuff about vegetables: you must be expert in these bulbs to cultivate them

explanation.surface: Expertise is needed to cultivate a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: To know your onions is a British idiom meaning to be expert in a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom about being knowledgeable names these vegetable bulbs, which a gardener grows.

clue.text: Washes surface of contact lens one's split

indicators.note: the surface of a word is its outermost, first letter
split means the word lens is broken open by one

parts.note: A is one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A contact lens that splits is washed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surface of' takes C from 'contact'; 'split' puts A (one) into LENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean something is to wash it, and the third-person form matches.

clue.text: College lecturers take worried artist to one side

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college

indicators.note: take means the lecturers hold the other pieces between them

parts.note: L is lecturer, doubled for the plural as in pp for pages
ate in the sense of worried or troubled, as in what ate you
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: University staff take a troubled painter aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' signals a container: the doubled L for lecturers holds the other two pieces. 'worried' as ATE is the old sense of something eating at you.
explanation.definitionFit: Unilateral means one-sided, done by or affecting only one party.

clue.text: El Dorado's gold gone? What's left could still make you rich

indicators.note: the letters remaining are then reshuffled into a new word
gone means the gold is taken out of the mythical city's name

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Even after its gold has gone, the legendary city could still make you wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' takes OR from ELDORADO, leaving ELDADO, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very rich, so being so means having a lot of money.

clue.text: Not as much activity in class?

parts.note: less means not as much
on means happening, in action

explanation.surface: There is less activity in a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, a class.

clue.text: Patrol leader passes round bread

indicators.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words, passing round it

explanation.surface: The scout patrol leader hands out the bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the two words patROL Leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a small individual loaf of bread.

clue.text: Cook, equivocating, having binned messy gite food

indicators.note: to cook something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook hedges and throws out the messy holiday cottage food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having binned messy gite' removes the letters G, I, T, E in any order from EQUIVOCATING; 'Cook' rearranges the rest. A gite is a French holiday cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken cooked in red wine is a classic French dish.

clue.text: Staircase with rails winding around post

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
winding means twisting, so the letters of rails are twisted around

explanation.surface: A staircase whose handrails wind around a central post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges RAILS into SIRAL, placed 'around' P.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral is a staircase winding round a central column, as in spiral staircase.

clue.text: Detect, say, aromas

indicators.note: say means spoken out loud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: senses means detects

explanation.surface: Detect, for example, various smells.
explanation.definitionFit: Scents are smells, especially pleasant ones.

clue.text: Directors and cast appear on them

definitions.meaning: company directors sit on the board
actors are said to tread the stage

explanation.surface: Executives and actors both appear on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Boards are company directors collectively, and also the theatre stage.
